_note: Fact-level sensitivity. A fact listed here NEVER reaches the writer — not as a hook, not as support, not as lineage. It stays in its dossier as a record of what the source said; only its REACH is removed. research/dossier.py applies this; WRITER_REACHABLE_SENSITIVITIES is a positive filter, so an unanticipated value is excluded by construction.
_agent_may_never: THE AGENT MAY NEVER ADD, EDIT, OR APPROVE AN ENTRY. approved_by is set by Ashton, by hand. Terms are used only to SURFACE candidates for his review — a regex does not decide this. The 2026-09-12 surfacing pass over 250 dossiers returned 8 candidates of which 5 were FALSE POSITIVES ('given a treatment of white paint', three 'low-light conditions', 'post-game recovery'), which is the argument against letting a pattern decide.
_matching: An entry is matched to a fact by (image_name, whitespace-collapsed text). NOT by fact id: ids are positional (f1, f2 ...) and shift the moment the tagger changes, which would silently move a flag onto a different sentence. dossier.py's main() FAILS LOUDLY if an entry here matches no fact — a flag that has lost its target must never fail open.
